en: When a plant's leaves absorb sunlight, chlorophyll converts water and carbon dioxide into glucose for energy.
A carabao's four-chambered stomach allows beneficial bacteria to break down tough grass cellulose into usable nutrients.
When the heart's ventricles contract, they pump oxygen-rich blood through the aorta to the rest of the body.
Tree roots absorb groundwater, which then travels up the trunk and evaporates from leaves through transpiration.
A stick insect's twig-like body shape prevents predators from seeing it, allowing the insect to survive longer.
During a butterfly's pupa stage, caterpillar tissues completely break down and reorganize into adult wings and antennae.
When a virus enters the body, white blood cells produce specific antibodies to destroy the invading pathogen.
A burdock seed's hooked spines attach to animal fur, allowing the plant to spread its offspring far away.
As water flows over a fish's gills, thin blood vessels absorb dissolved oxygen directly from the water.
When you touch a hot stove, sensory nerves send electrical signals to your brain to trigger muscle withdrawal.
When a bee collects nectar, pollen sticks to its fuzzy body and transfers to the next flower's stigma.
A cactus's thick stem stores water during heavy rains, allowing the plant to survive long dry desert periods.
